problem_statement: SIH26085 Urban Flood Nowcasting System (MoES / NCMRWF)

local_lows.rule: local low: a non-outfall junction whose street level is below that of every junction it shares a segment with. Closed depression: street level below the lowest level at which water could spill along street segments to an outfall (priority-flood fill from the outfalls). Deep: peak street depth over deep_m in any exported scenario.

sources.name: Greater Chennai Corporation storm-water drain survey (routes, inverts, sizes, condition)
Chennai 2015 flood records: stagnation points, inundation depths, crowd-mapped flooded streets
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, tile N13 E080
OpenStreetMap waterways (canals, rivers, drains, streams) via Overpass (outfalls)

storm.kind: synthetic, spatially uniform over the site
storm.shape: bell-shaped (Gaussian) in time, generated by jaldrishti.model.storm

model: Local-inertial flow in drains and 1D street channels along them, Preissmann-style slot for surcharge, weir and orifice exchange at inlets, silt raises the drain bed. JAX, differentiable.
gcc_drain_id_note: gcc_drain is the row index of the drain in the processed GCC survey (data/processed/drains.json), the id used in results/. survey_objectid is the OBJECTID in the GCC KML.
pooling_note: With a 30 m DEM and 1D streets, water pools at street low points: 93 of 406 junctions sit lower than every neighbour. All 20 junctions where street depth passes 1 m in any scenario lie in closed street depressions, below the level at which water could spill along the streets to an outfall. Treat depths over 1 m as model artifacts until the model is calibrated.
caveats: Rain in every flood scenario is a synthetic storm, spatially uniform over the site. It is not a radar nowcast.
Hydraulic parameters (Manning roughness, inlet size and spacing, catchment width) are assumed values, not calibrated against observed floods.
The street surface is modelled as 1D street channels along the surveyed drains. It is not a 2D grid.

With a 30 m DEM and 1D streets, water pools at street low points: 93 of 406 junctions sit lower than every neighbour. All 20 junctions where street depth passes 1 m in any scenario lie in closed street depressions, below the level at which water could spill along the streets to an outfall. Treat depths over 1 m as model artifacts until the model is calibrated.
Silted and inferred drain states come from an identical-twin test: silt was planted in the model. They are not field findings.
The twin test uses the same model and the same known rain for the truth and the inversion.
The radar demo uses Mumbai frames because the Chennai radar was offline on 2026-09-24.
Outfalls are free. Canal and tide backwater is not modelled.
Street level comes from the 30 m Copernicus DEM, which is coarse for streets.
